project_name: AquaBounty Pioneer property data center infrastructure review
developer: AquaBounty Technologies; future buyer/developer not selected
status_detail: AquaBounty's August 6, 2026 Form 8-K/press release says it expanded the strategic alternatives review for its Pioneer, Ohio property to include power infrastructure and energy development opportunities. The site has about 50 MW of available substation capacity and a 5.25 million gallons/day groundwater withdrawal permit, and the company says these attributes could support data center infrastructure, but no transaction or data center developer is assured.
notes: Included under 宁多勿漏 as an announced site-reuse/strategic-review lead rather than a committed data center project. County official site links WEDCO as economic development contact; no county approval for a data center found in this pass.

status_detail: Meta announced on April 9, 2025 that Middleton Township would host a 715,000-square-foot Meta-owned and operated data center campus representing more than $800 million in investment and about 100 jobs. Local and county materials show the project received a 75% property-tax abatement for 15 years in 2023, with continuing 2026 public concern and planning commission discussion while construction proceeds.
notes: Meta's own announcement and Middleton Township page are primary evidence. Capacity in MW was not found in official accessible sources; local reports describe a related power-plant controversy but not a public Meta campus MW figure.

project_name: Smartland Energy Upper Sandusky data center and power project
status_detail: Local reporting and public notices describe Smartland Energy's similar-use petition for a proposed Upper Sandusky project with a large-scale computing/data center component and a 150 MW dedicated natural-gas power generation facility on about 146 acres. Daily Chief-Union reported on June 29, 2026 that Smartland Energy voluntarily withdrew the similar-use petition; status is mapped to rejected because the allowed enum lacks withdrawn.
notes: County and WCOED official pages were checked for coverage. Specific project facts come from local news/commentary quoting the petition and city process; no fully accessible official packet was found in this pass.

project_name: Atoka / Kiowa hyperscale data center lead
aliases: Tokyo Energy Park and data center
Atoka County data center north of Atoka
developer: Unknown; social posts mention IREN but not verified
status_detail: Searches surfaced local social-media discussion of a data center north of Atoka and speculation that a Pittsburg County/Atoka County project could locate in either county. A Crexi listing for 1302 Reynolds Rd, Kiowa, OK markets 286 acres in Atoka County as an industrial development opportunity near Kiowa Power Plant, substations, water and fiber routes to an Equinix Dallas data center, but the listing is not itself proof of an active data center project. No official Atoka County approval, permit, abatement, or named developer was found.
notes: Kept as a low-confidence lead under 宁多勿漏. Treat IREN/50B/Tokyo Energy Park references as unverified until an Atoka County record, utility filing, or credible local article confirms the project.

project_name: Choctaw Nation of Oklahoma Data Center
aliases: Choctaw Nation Data Center and Emergency Operations Center
status_detail: FSB's project page says it worked with the Choctaw Nation of Oklahoma on a dual-purpose building housing the Choctaw Nation Data Center and Emergency Operations Center in Durant, and says the completed center supports the headquarters campus. CRUX Solutions lists the Choctaw Nation Data Center in Durant as 14,500 sf with November 2017 completion. DCMAP lists Choctaw Nation of Oklahoma Data Center in Durant as operational.
notes: Original A/E and low-voltage contractor pages provide detailed project evidence; DCMAP confirms county/state tracker presence. Capacity not publicly available.

aliases: SmartTec Mead Oklahoma Data Center Site
status_detail: SmartTec's site page describes a pre-launch data center/AI compute site in Mead, Bryan County on US-70, with 30 owned acres, three existing 3,000-square-foot buildings, a 3 MVA on-site transformer, a signed 100 Gbps fiber quote, and Phase 1A targeting power-on in Q4 2026 at about 114 kW IT load. SmartTec states the compute does not exist yet.
notes: Small pre-launch AI compute project; included because the developer provides project-specific site, power, and schedule details. Not yet operational as of source text.
